items.title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
items.summary: Phronix introduces a capability-centric learning paradigm for agents to acquire, validate, and refine reusable skills from their own executions. It operates via a predictor-validator-corrector loop where proposed solutions are validated by tool executions, and outcomes refine stored capabilities. This process results in learned capabilities that solve recurring tasks on the first attempt with high accuracy, reducing solution non-determinism. Phronix efficiently generates durable capabilities from agent executions and significantly reduces the token cost for warm-start runs. Empirical results show Phronix improves task-solving rates and performance in complex performance engineering workflows.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents" details a capability-centric learning framework for agents that acquires and refines reusable skills through execution validation. This system operates using a predictor-validator-corrector loop where proposed solutions are tested via tool executions, and the resulting outcomes are used to refine stored capabilities. This process yields learned capabilities that solve recurring tasks with high accuracy on the initial attempt, thereby reducing solution non-determinism and efficiently generating durable skills from agent executions. Empirical findings indicate that Phronix improves task-solving rates and performance within complex performance engineering workflows while significantly reducing the token cost for warm-start runs. This advancement points toward more robust and efficient autonomous agent development.

items.title: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
items.summary: Intelligent agents require a method to learn from mistakes to achieve continuous improvement, as current in-context reflection and fine-tuning methods are inefficient. Self-Direction introduces a mechanism where agents reflect on failures to extract lessons and distill them into lightweight low-rank adapters. This process keeps base model weights frozen, training only a small percentage of adapter parameters. Learned lessons are stored in a persistent library, allowing adapters to be automatically applied to solve related future problems. Experiments demonstrated that Self-Direction significantly improved agent success rates and fostered the transfer of learned knowledge across diverse tasks.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons" details a method where intelligent agents learn from failures to achieve continuous improvement. This research introduces a mechanism called Self-Direction that allows agents to reflect on mistakes, extract lessons, and distill them into lightweight low-rank adapters without altering the base model weights. The process involves storing learned lessons in a persistent library, enabling these adapters to be automatically applied to solve subsequent, related problems. Experiments showed that this approach significantly improved agent success rates and facilitated the transfer of knowledge across different tasks. This development points toward a new paradigm for training advanced AI systems through self-correction and knowledge retention.

items.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
items.summary: The study investigates the execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, focusing on recovery decisions separate from language-model behavior. It defines distinct obligations for a durable agent, including checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of external effects, and permission to reconcile. A finite conformance study was conducted across multiple histories on LangGraph and Temporal hosts, checking these obligations. Results indicate that cached retry, revalidation before retry, and stable-key retry successfully pass a portion of the recorded histories. Furthermore, a component study on an enterprise AI platform isolated the roles of authority, provider contracts, and observations in recovery scenarios.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows" investigates the execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents by defining specific obligations for a durable agent related to checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of external effects, and permission to reconcile, finding that specific retry mechanisms successfully pass a portion of recorded histories. The study conducted a finite conformance examination across multiple histories utilizing LangGraph and Temporal hosts to check these defined obligations. Results demonstrated that cached retry, revalidation before retry, and stable-key retry successfully passed a segment of the recorded histories. A component study further isolated the roles of authority, provider contracts, and observations within enterprise AI platform recovery scenarios. This research establishes formal requirements for reliable AI agent operation and recovery protocols in complex workflows.

items.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
items.summary: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is harmful language that belittles vulnerable groups by assuming pity and reinforcing negative stereotypes. The research proposes automated systems to detect this type of language in both English and Mandarin. Two detection approaches were tested: one used static word embeddings and a convolutional neural network, and the second used fine-tuned pre-trained BERT embeddings. The BERT-based approach proved more successful, achieving an F1 score of 0.528 on the development set. This work addresses the difficulty humans have in detecting PCL despite its harmful nature.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin" reports on the development of automated systems for identifying patronizing and condescending language in both English and Mandarin. The research demonstrated that a BERT-based approach proved more successful in detecting this type of harmful language, achieving an F1 score of 0.528 on the development set. The study tested two detection methodologies: one utilized static word embeddings combined with a convolutional neural network, and the second employed fine-tuned pre-trained BERT embeddings. The BERT-based method yielded superior performance, addressing the known difficulty humans face in accurately recognizing the harmful nature of such language. This research indicates progress in applying machine learning to identify subtle forms of linguistic harm across different languages.

items.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
items.summary: PaperFormalizer is a Lean-based agentic pipeline designed to automatically formalize research papers by authors. It processes LaTeX source material into a dependency graph, audits statements for correctness and ambiguity, and formalizes them using Lean and Mathlib. The process involves interactive steps where the author reviews and approves proposed formalizations. The system generates an annotated paper, a change report, and linked Lean code. This aims to make research based on mathematical proofs more robust and shareable.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean". This story concerns a Lean-based agentic pipeline designed to automatically formalize research papers by authors through an interactive process. The system processes LaTeX source material into a dependency graph, audits statements for correctness and ambiguity, and formalizes them using Lean and Mathlib, requiring author review and approval at each step. The process generates an annotated paper, a change report, and linked Lean code, aiming to increase the robustness and shareability of research based on mathematical proofs. This technology demonstrates a method for integrating formal mathematical reasoning directly into the research documentation workflow. Further development in this area suggests advancements in automated verification and knowledge representation systems.

items.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
items.summary: $M^3$ is a multi-LLM framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process. It uses a state LLM to maintain a compact internal state while an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM. Empirical results show $M^3$ significantly outperforms state-of-the-art multi-turn red-teaming methods in Attack Success Rates (ASR). The system demonstrates improved effectiveness and more consistent performance across risk categories without requiring predefined taxonomies. This provides a scalable and principled approach for multi-turn safety evaluation.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "$M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process" details a multi-LLM framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process and demonstrates superior performance in attack success rates. The research introduces $M^3$, a framework that employs a state LLM to maintain an internal state while an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM in a multi-turn setting. This methodology frames the interaction as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process, allowing the system to manage the state effectively during the adversarial exchange. Empirical evaluations indicate that the $M^3$ system significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art multi-turn red-teaming methods in terms of Attack Success Rates. Furthermore, the system exhibits improved effectiveness and more consistent performance across various risk categories without reliance on predefined taxonomies for evaluation. This work establishes a scalable and principled approach for multi-turn safety assessment in large language models. The findings suggest a new formal structure for assessing adversarial vulnerability in conversational AI systems.

items.title: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation
items.summary: LLM agents in repeated multi-party negotiations face challenges due to a gap between knowing who to trust and reaching an agreement. The research investigates whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions to improve future outcomes. A framework is introduced where agents assess pairwise trust after each negotiation game to account for adversaries. Results show a trust-agreement gap, indicating that trust estimates do not always lead to better agreements on their own. Explicit guidance on using trust can increase agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" investigates the challenges faced by LLM agents in repeated multi-party negotiations due to a gap between knowing who to trust and actually reaching an agreement. The research introduced a framework where agents assess pairwise trust following each negotiation game to account for adversaries. Results demonstrated a trust-agreement gap, indicating that trust estimates alone do not reliably lead to improved agreements. Explicit guidance on the utilization of trust was shown to increase agreement rates by up to twenty-three percentage points. This finding suggests that incorporating explicit trust management is a necessary component for effective multi-party LLM negotiation systems.

items.title: Beyond On-Policy vs. Off-Policy: At What Level Should LLM Agent Distillation Follow the Student?
items.summary: Distilling interactive LLM agents requires choosing between on-policy and off-policy distillation, which corresponds to teacher-generated demonstrations versus student-generated experience. The authors propose a hierarchical agent distillation framework to explicitly control the pairing, mixture proportions, and training schedule of these two levels of on-policiness. Empirical study suggests that student-induced histories paired with teacher action prefixes offer the strongest standalone training signal. Following the student at both levels generally performs poorly, although mixtures can be beneficial. Practical principles are derived for determining where, how much, and when agent distillation should follow the student.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Beyond On-Policy vs. Off-Policy: At What Level Should LLM Agent Distillation?" explores the optimal approach for distilling interactive large language model agents by examining on-policy versus off-policy distillation. The research proposes a hierarchical agent distillation framework to manage the pairing, mixture proportions, and training schedule between teacher-generated demonstrations and student-generated experience. Empirical study indicated that student-induced histories paired with teacher action prefixes provided the strongest standalone training signal during the distillation process. Following the student at both levels generally resulted in suboptimal performance, although mixtures of these signals demonstrated potential benefits. These findings establish practical principles for determining the appropriate timing and extent of agent distillation. The results offer guidance for designing more effective agent training methodologies in the field.

items.title: Tradeoff-Aware Territory Design: A Multi-Objective Decision System for Enterprise Customer-to-Seller Allocation
items.summary: A production decision system is presented for trade-aware customer-to-seller allocation in enterprise go-to-market planning. It integrates a multidimensional account-value layer, an observational continuity-valuation layer, and a multi-objective optimization layer. This framework allows planners to inspect and compare allocation tradeoffs among growth, balance, capacity, and feasibility. Historical backtesting demonstrated that optimizer-generated scenarios improved assignment compliance while maintaining opportunity distribution. Ultimately, the system guides the allocation of scarce seller capacity toward higher-value accounts for increased revenue potential.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Tradeoff-Aware Territory Design: A Multi-Objective Decision System for Enterprise Customer-to-Seller Allocation" presents a production decision system for trade-aware customer-to-seller allocation in enterprise go-to-market planning, demonstrating that the system guides the allocation of scarce seller capacity toward higher-value accounts for increased revenue potential. The framework integrates a multidimensional account-value layer, an observational continuity-valuation layer, and a multi-objective optimization layer to facilitate the inspection and comparison of allocation tradeoffs across growth, balance, capacity, and feasibility. Historical backtesting indicated that scenarios generated by the optimizer enhanced assignment compliance while preserving opportunity distribution. This methodology systematically directs the allocation of limited seller capacity based on assessed account value to maximize revenue outcomes. This research contributes to the development of sophisticated decision-making systems for complex enterprise resource management.

items.title: Batched NN 4D-Var: a performant hybrid model framework for the Integrated Forecasting System
items.summary: The research investigates online learning of state-dependent model-error corrections within the Integrated Forecasting System using 4D-Var. It proposes a batched extension for this approach, processing assimilation windows in random order and averaging parameter increments like in mini-batch optimization. Experiments show that the batched formulation consistently improves forecast skill in out-of-sample tests, unlike sequential online learning which fails to generalize. Larger batch sizes enhance convergence and robustness by mitigating parameter update noise. The findings suggest that the formulation of the online learning problem is crucial for generalization in hybrid machine-learning/data-assimilation systems.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Batched NN 4D-Var: a performant hybrid model framework for the Integrated Forecasting System" investigates online learning of state-dependent model-error corrections within the Integrated Forecasting System using 4D-Var and demonstrates that a batched extension consistently improves forecast skill in out-of-sample tests compared to sequential online learning. The research proposes a batched extension for this approach by processing assimilation windows in random order and averaging parameter increments similar to mini-batch optimization. Experiments reveal that the batched formulation achieves superior forecast skill, while sequential online learning exhibits a failure to generalize. Larger batch sizes were shown to enhance convergence and robustness by reducing parameter update noise. The findings indicate that the specific formulation of the online learning problem is critical for generalization in hybrid machine-learning and data-assimilation systems. This work points toward a necessary framework for robust generalization in integrating machine learning with data assimilation techniques.

items.title: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
items.summary: TACS-RF presents a framework for tool-driven, agentic circuit synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. A large-language model agent drives industry-standard EDA tools like Cadence and Ansys HFSS to perform the design. The framework was validated by the agent designing a 240-251 GHz sub-THz transmitter on a 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS process. The agent autonomously designed complex sub-blocks including VCOs, power drivers, and antenna structures. The resulting design achieved +5.1 to +6.3 dBm output power with specified phase noise and power consumption.

items.title: Autoregressive Physics-Informed Neural Operator Surrogates and Joint 4-D Seismic-Production Bayesian History Matching
items.summary: A surrogate-accelerated Bayesian history-matching framework is presented for joint 4-D seismic and production data assimilation. It employs an autoregressive Physics-Informed Neural Operator (PINO) to model the forward map, incorporating black-oil residuals as a penalty. Adaptive regularised ensemble Kalman inversion (aREKI) is used to assimilate data, followed by an ensemble smoother for joint estimation. The method ensures stability and tractability by carefully constraining the inversion space, leading to significant computational speed-ups. The approach demonstrates high accuracy and efficiency in history matching.

items.title: Federated Nonparametric Regression with Heterogeneous Clients
items.summary: The study investigates federated nonparametric regression for clients with heterogeneous data distributions and estimation uncertainties. It addresses whether a federated predictor benefits an individual client based on population heterogeneity and uncertainty. The method allows clients to transmit local kernel summaries so the server can construct a covariate-density-weighted estimator without centralizing individual data. Client gains are characterized, and the framework provides pointwise inference for the federated estimator. Robustness is analyzed under perturbation models, using Kullback-Leibler and $L_2$ neighborhoods to assess variance-sensitive and exact fitting properties.

items.title: Acquisition for Spherical-Linear Bayesian Optimization on the Cube
items.summary: A method using a linear surrogate approximates Gaussian Process performance in high-dimensional test functions. While this approach yields exact acquisition for spherical decision regions, the unit cube is more common in Bayesian Optimization. The paper investigates the complexity of globally solving acquisition subproblems over the unit cube using standard multi-start quasi-Newton methods. A new acquisition function is proposed that is globally optimizable faster than existing methods while maintaining or improving performance. This resulting method is competitive with GP-based BO in accuracy per evaluation and superior in accuracy per walltime.

items.title: Empirical concentration for chains with infinite memory
items.summary: The work establishes empirical concentration inequalities for stationary chains with infinite memory, extending previous results from Markov chains. It develops a bounded-differences inequality on bounded Polish metric spaces using a summable Wasserstein contraction condition. Dependence coefficients are estimated from a single trajectory using transition counts or kernel conditional-density estimates. The procedure yields empirical concentration bounds that are asymptotically as tight as their theoretical counterparts. These bounds are fully adaptive, requiring no prior knowledge of the inequality's constants.

items.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons
items.summary: A neural exploratory framework is proposed for variational problems over graphons, which are limits of dense graph sequences. Graphons are represented by implicit neural networks, and objective optimization is performed using gradient descent. The framework incorporates a multi-scale residual architecture, an embedded solver enforcing density constraints, and symmetry-aware Monte Carlo estimators. This method successfully finds optimal graphons for generalized Turán problems and variational problems from large deviation theory. The work yields new candidate optima and theorems regarding optimal graphons for these problems.

items.title: Conditional Flow Models for Offline Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Offline maximum entropy reinforcement learning estimates the optimal soft action-value function $Q^*$ from fixed datasets without further interaction. The proposed framework uses conditional diffusion models based on probability flow ODEs to estimate the conditional reward distribution and transition kernel. These distributional estimators approximate the soft optimal Bellman operator, which is then minimized over deep neural networks to estimate $Q^*$. The method establishes nonasymptotic guarantees for operator learning and value learning, providing an excess Bellman residual risk bound. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical effectiveness of this approach.

items.title: Exact Global Minimax Risk near Nonidentification
items.summary: The study investigates squared-error estimation when a nuisance parameter is unidentified in a submodel affecting a target that vanishes there. Sufficient conditions are provided for the largest critical-path minimax risk to equal the exact asymptotic minimax risk over the full parameter space when using higher-order profile expansions. An estimator achieving the leading constant uniformly is possible under conditions involving efficient observable features and stable recovery. The method employs calibration estimates, a local feature mean, and an empirical recovery feature. The results are verified in models involving logistic errors-in-variables regression and replicated-network models.

items.title: Early learning in large residual networks
items.summary: The study examines the early training dynamics of nonlinear residual networks modeled with zero hidden layers to understand general residual networks. The research uses a sequential limit where network width, depth, training data size, and input dimension all diverge. A key finding is that in the limit of large input dimension, the network output can only learn a linear function of inputs early in training. This suggests that mean-field limits of ResNets are rigid and may be insufficient for feature learning in high-dimensional regimes. The work also investigates methods for transferring learning rate hyperparameter based on dataset size and input dimension.

items.title: Combinatorial Characterizations of the Learnability of Conditional Distributions
items.summary: The paper investigates the PAC-learnability of function classes mapping inputs to conditional probability distributions over a finite space. It introduces the fat$_\gamma$Natarajan dimension, which is shown to be a necessary and sufficient condition for learnability when finite at every positive scale. A fat$_\gamma$Graph dimension is also introduced, along with inequalities comparing it to the former, establishing an equivalent characterization of learnability. The authors further demonstrate that a distribution-valued function class is learnable if and only if its coordinate classes are learnable in the probabilistic concept model.
